l: retrieval augmented generation with LLMs, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
s: Retrieval augmented generation with LLMs retrieves passages and sometimes knowledge graph triples to reduce hallucination and improve factuality, including revising decomposed chain-of-thought steps; it culminates in a training framework that produces more robust retrievers and improves retrieval and generation over a baseline.

l: question, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
s: The question serves as input for retrieval and response generation: a retriever encodes and compares it with passages, then combines it with retrieved passages into a knowledge representation.

l: knowledge source, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
s: is_a passage corpus The knowledge source is the passage corpus from which question-relevant passages are retrieved.

l: question-relevant passages, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
s: is_retrieved_from passage corpus [as question-relevant passages Pq ⊂P] Question-relevant passages are passages in the passage corpus that are relevant to the question. Knowledge-relevant passages and label-relevant passages are subsets of them.

l: natural language response, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
s: The natural language response is generated conditioned on the question and the retrieved question-relevant passages. The answer is encoded to provide a rich representation of the knowledge needed to reconstruct it. In Retriever as Answer Classifier, positive and in-batch negative answers are scored against the retrieved passages.

l: retrieval step, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
s: is_unavailable available [during training] The retrieval step selects question-relevant passages from the passage corpus. Because these passages are unavailable during training, state-of-the-art works marginalize this step.

l: knowledge, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
s: Knowledge is information in knowledge-relevant passages enabling label-answer generation. It is represented as a dense bottleneck encoding from answers or question-passage pairs, guiding retrieval toward information relevant to answering questions.

l: training, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
s: Training uses the negative log-likelihood loss to train the retriever and generator. Standard training biases the retriever toward label-relevant passages, while the proposed approach focuses on knowledge-relevant passages.

l: training framework, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
s: This training framework for knowledge-intensive generation tasks trains a retriever to seek knowledge-relevant passages rather than only label-relevant ones, aiming for greater robustness and generalization. It uses RAG as a retrieve-generate encoder-decoder backbone and combines generation loss with two knowledge-constrained objectives: Retriever as Answer Classifier (RAC) and Dense Knowledge Similarity (DKS). In multi-task training, it optimizes generation, answer-classification, and knowledge-similarity losses, with a weight vector computed at each step so the losses have the same value. It is evaluated in retrieval, end-to-end generation, combined evaluation, and robustness, against RAG and non-finetuned DPR. The reported methods improve retrieval and generation metrics on MSMARCO and KILT Wizard of Wikipedia, outperform RAG in retrieval, and show lower overfitting, especially on KILT-WoW. Reported KILT-WoW results include 13.3% relative improvement on KILT-RL and 13.2% on KILT-F1 over baseline RAG. By guiding retrieval toward knowledge-relevant passages, it mitigates overfitting and can reduce hallucinations when training retrievers for large language models.

l: sentence bottleneck auto-encoder, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
s: Sentence bottleneck auto-encoder extracts answer knowledge representations by using a frozen pre-trained encoder, aggregating its states with multihead attention into one bottleneck representation, then reconstructing the answer through that representation.

l: label sentence, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
s: The label sentence is the target output whose probability the generation objective maximizes. Its negative log-likelihood is used as the generation loss.

l: passage, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
s: A passage is encoded and scored for similarity with a question. Retrieved passages are concatenated with the question for generation and contribute probability-weighted representations to the knowledge objectives.

l: multi-task, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
s: This proposed multi-task method is evaluated as a variant on MSMARCO and KILT-WoW. It performs best overall on MSMARCO, with the highest retrieval recalls and 55.1 BLEU-1, 34.8 BLEU-4, 59.1 ROUGE-L, and 50.5 METEOR. It reports 12.0 Recall@1 on MSMARCO development and 19.04 end-to-end F1 on KILT-WoW, improves Recall@1 over non-finetuned DPR, but misses the gold passage in the Gouda cheese case.

l: ROUGE-L, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
s: It is used to evaluate end-to-end generation for MSMARCO and KILT-WoW, and it also contributes to the KILT-RL combined metric. The multi-task method obtains 59.1 ROUGE-L on MSMARCO, while RAC obtains 16.81 ROUGE-L on KILT-WoW among the listed methods.

l: METEOR, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
s: It is reported for both datasets as a metric intended to correlate highly with human judgment and mimic human preferences for generations. The multi-task method obtains 50.5 on MSMARCO, while RAC obtains 14.47 on KILT-WoW.

l: KILT-F1, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
s: calculates F1 score [as 0 when the retriever does not perfectly select the gold passage] KILT-F1 is used in the KILT-WoW leaderboard evaluation. The proposed methods achieve a 13.2% relative improvement over RAG on KILT-F1.

l: RQ1: Effectiveness, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
s: RQ1: Effectiveness is evaluated through retrieval, end-to-end generation, and combined metrics on MSMARCO and KILT-WoW. The proposed methods consistently outperform RAG, with improvements in retrieval and generation.

l: RQ2: Robustness, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
s: RQ2: Robustness evaluates overfit through train-to-development metric differences, measuring retrieval performance drops; proposed methods generally drop less than RAG, especially on KILT-WoW.

l: Gouda cheese, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
s: Gouda cheese is a mild, yellow cheese, one of the oldest recorded cheeses still made today. It was mentioned as early as 1184 and is the subject of a KILT-WoW case study.

l: baseline model, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
s: is_compared_with training framework [on retrieval and generation metrics] The baseline model is used for comparison in the experiments. The proposed methods outperform it on retrieval and generation metrics on MSMARCO and KILT Wizard of Wikipedia.

l: retrieval augmentation, Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
s: Retrieval augmentation is crucial for large language models, supports complex reasoning, faces knowledge-editing challenges, and may combine passages with databases and knowledge graphs.
